rules.description: A supply record has exactly one supplier.
A supply record has exactly one immediate buyer.
An opportunity has exactly one prospective seller.
An opportunity has exactly one target customer.
A collaboration has at least two participants.
An assessment compares exactly one offering A…
…with exactly one offering B.
An assessment is scoped to exactly one market segment.
Offering A and offering B must differ.
Relationship records must cite at least one Evidence node.

Each complete CompetitionAssessment projects a product-level link (DIRECTLY/INDIRECTLY_COMPETES_WITH) and company-level links (DIRECT/INDIRECT_COMPETITOR_OF) between the companies that SELL or BRAND the two offerings. Projections inherit verification, evidence and overlap_scope.
Every pair of Company participants of a Collaboration gets a COLLABORATES_WITH link carrying the collaboration stage.

SupplyRelationship at design_win, mass_production or unspecified stage projects SUPPLIES_TO; at prospect, qualified or sampling it projects MAY_SUPPLY_TO. Open CustomerOpportunity records also project MAY_SUPPLY_TO. Ended links are not projected.
A company is ACTIVE_IN_SEGMENT of every segment its offerings target (TARGETS_SEGMENT, or IN_CATEGORY → CATEGORY_IN_SEGMENT).
Every company sells at least one offering (product, service or business line).
Every company sits in at least one market segment (directly or via its offerings).
Every offering is placed in a segment or category.
Every product category belongs to a segment.
Every market segment belongs to an industry.
Two unrelated companies sell the same offering → possible competitors.
Offerings of two companies are in the same product category → possible competitors.
Offerings of two companies target the same market segment → possible competitors.
Offerings of two companies are built on the same technology → possible competitors on that platform.
A company's offering is built on a technology another company provides → possible supplier.
A company works in a segment that feeds another company's segment → possible supplier.
